title: Insider PowerToys version tricks the Microsoft store into thinking that PowerToys is not installed
author: ReginaldTang

judgment.rationale: The stable-to-Insider transition is a concrete packaging scenario and a repository fix may be applicable, but no package identity/version data or reproduction log is attached.
evidence: The report says an Insider 0.101.2432 build was installed from Microsoft Store.
The Store subsequently shows PowerToys as not installed.
The issue has no comments, assignee, duplicate, or linked fix.
Installer code contains a sparse Package Identity MSIX registration path, while Store recognition depends on package identity and registration.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the controlled stable-to-Insider reproduction and compare package identity, family name, registration, and upgrade metadata; use the proposed packaging design only if the identity change is confirmed.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt is linked; the installer/package-identity code is applicable, but the report does not prove whether the Insider package identity changed intentionally or registration is incomplete.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Store-recognizable package identity across Insider upgrades
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the Insider package or sparse package registration presents a package identity/version/channel combination that Microsoft Store does not associate with the stable product, or the upgrade leaves the sparse identity registration incomplete. The report does not yet distinguish identity mismatch from an intentional preview-channel limitation.
plan: Reproduce from Store stable to Insider and record Package Full Name, Family Name, application identity, install location, and Store page state before and after.
Inspect the Insider and stable manifests/build variables and the installer InstallPackageIdentityMSIXCA registration path for changes to package family, publisher, identity, or upgrade behavior.

If the identity should remain compatible, keep the stable Store identity and version-compatible registration across the channel transition; if Insider is intentionally a separate product, document the limitation instead of changing identity unsafely.
Add packaging validation that compares identity fields and verifies upgrade/registration behavior for stable-to-Insider and Insider-to-stable transitions.
verification: Install Store stable, confirm Store recognizes it, install the current Insider build, restart Store, and verify the page still recognizes the installed product.
Inspect package identity and registration before and after; confirm no unrelated package is removed or orphaned.
Verify rollback or upgrade back to stable remains supported.

confidence.rationale: Package identity is the likely boundary, but the issue provides only a screenshot and no before/after identity data.

issue_context.summary: After updating to an Insider PowerToys build, Microsoft Store offers installation instead of recognizing PowerToys as installed.
known_information: The affected build is 0.101.2432 Insider and the installation method is Microsoft Store.
The symptom follows an update to the Insider release.
The issue has no comments, attachments, assignee, or linked remediation.
The installer contains explicit sparse Package Identity MSIX install/uninstall custom actions.
inferences: A package family, publisher, identity, version, or registration transition may be outside the Store's expected upgrade relationship.
The behavior could instead be an intentional separation of Insider and stable Store products.
issue_context.analysis: A controlled package inspection can decide whether this is a fixable registration regression or expected channel behavior. The design therefore names the exact installer boundary but keeps confidence red until identity evidence exists.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, labels, timeline state, and absence of linked work.
Inspected installer Package Identity MSIX registration and uninstall code in CustomAction.cpp and Product.wxs.
Searched related Store/package identity reports and found no direct linked fix for this issue.

information_gaps.information: Stable and Insider Package Full Name, Family Name, publisher, version, and registration state.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether Store recognition failed because identity changed or because registration/upgrade state is incomplete.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On a test machine, record Get-AppxPackage and Store state before stable-to-Insider installation and after restarting Microsoft Store.

information_gaps.information: Whether Insider and stable are intended to share Store ownership.
information_gaps.why_needed: Avoids changing package identity when the preview channel is intentionally a separate Store product.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the supported channel transition and expected Store behavior in the current release/packaging documentation.

design.root_cause: Unconfirmed. The leading hypothesis is a Store package identity or sparse-registration mismatch introduced during the stable-to-Insider transition; a controlled package comparison is required before calling it a defect.
evidence: [Observed] Store recognition is lost after installing an Insider build over the existing installation.
[Observed] No diagnostic package metadata or maintainer discussion is attached.
[Observed] Installer code installs a sparse Package Identity MSIX using the product's install folder and removes it through a fixed package family path.
[Inferred] Package identity, registration, or supported channel relationship is the correct investigation boundary.

affected_files.purpose: Installs and uninstalls sparse Package Identity MSIX registration.
Schedules Package Identity installation and removal during MSI install/upgrade.
Contains the stable/Insider manifest and packaging inputs whose identity fields must be compared.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The installer registers a sparse package during installation and removes the fixed sparse package family during uninstall; the issue's channel transition has not been validated here.
implementation_steps.change: After identity comparison, preserve compatible package identity and ensure upgrade registration is applied whenever the existing installation is upgraded, not only on a fresh install, while retaining per-user/machine scope handling.
implementation_steps.code_block:
before = identity + registration + Store state
install Insider
after = identity + registration + Store state
if identity should be shared: keep Name/Publisher/Family and register on upgrade
else: classify as expected channel behavior and do not alter identity
edge_cases: Stable and Insider may intentionally use different package identities.
Per-user and machine package registration must remain isolated.
Uninstall must not remove a package belonging to another channel or user.
Do not claim Store ownership when the Store product is intentionally separate.
tests: Validate manifest identity fields for both channels.
Run stable-to-Insider and Insider-to-stable package registration tests on a Windows test machine.
Verify Store recognition after Store restart.

verify: Record package identity and Store state before and after the controlled transition.
Run the narrowest existing installer/package validation command discovered during implementation.
Confirm Store recognizes the installed product when identities are intended to be shared, or document the intentional limitation when they are not.
risks: Changing package identity can strand installed packages or break Store updates for existing users.
Sparse package registration is tied to install scope and DACL behavior; careless changes can affect shell integration and uninstall.
alternatives: Tell users to uninstall/reinstall; rejected as it does not fix a compatible identity/registration regression.
Force Store cache refresh only; rejected because the symptom may be package identity or registration, not Store UI cache.
Treat Insider as always separate; retained as an explicit alternative until supported channel semantics are confirmed.

prerequisites: A Windows test environment with Microsoft Store access.
A clean stable Store PowerToys installation.
steps: Install PowerToys from Microsoft Store and record package identity and Store recognition.
Install the current Insider build over it.
Restart Microsoft Store and open the PowerToys page.
Record package identity, registration, and whether Store recognizes the installation.
If possible, upgrade back to stable and repeat the checks.
reproduce.expected_result: If stable and Insider are intended to share the product, Store continues to recognize the installed package; otherwise the supported preview-channel limitation is confirmed.
setup_requirements: Record installer type, architecture, stable version, Insider version, Package Full Name, Family Name, publisher, and install scope.
reproduce.version_requirement: Use the current Store stable release followed by the current Insider build.
